answer: AI agents managing walnut and tundra supply networks resist Sybil attacks through graph-based trust routing. Nodes accept transactions only along bounded random walks over reciprocal, cryptographically signed trust edges. An attacker seeking to forge influence incurs the verifiable cost of cultivating authentic, bilateral exchange histories with honest peers. A key limitation is that sparsely connected honest agents risk being misidentified as Sybil nodes and partitioned.
